title: Backpressure-aware kernel scheduling and ghost-recovery protocol for paged KV
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: Under mixed workloads (many short interactive chats + occasional long batched prefill), the paged KV cache sees sharp oscillations: aggressive prefill causes eviction storms, while concurrent decode waves create backpressure that leads to kernel queueing and tail-latency spikes. We need a scheduler that reasons about backpressure at the kernel layer and a lightweight ghost-recovery protocol to rehydrate useful fragments that were prematurely evicted.

Goal: Implement a backpressure-aware kernel prioritizer that: (1) defers or throttles low-value prefill waves when decode path queues approach SLO thresholds; (2) matches kernel candidates to fragment reuse potential (reuse score) to avoid thrashing; and (3) provides a ghost-recovery mechanism that marks recently-evicted fragments with a probabilistic tombstone to allow cheap on-demand rehydration without full prefill.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end e2e benchmark shows 25% reduction in 99th-percentile decode latency under mixed workload compared to baseline; 2) Overall token cost remains within 5% of baseline; 3) No regressions on single-stream latency tests; 4) Unit + integration tests for scheduler heuristics and ghost tombstone lifecycle included in CI; 5) Feature flag gated rollout with telemetry (prefill-throttled, kernel-priority decisions, ghost-cache-hits) available in Console.
design_notes:
- Scoring: compute a lightweight reuse_score per fragment using last_touch_time, access_frequency, and estimated rehydration_cost. Use exponential decay on frequency to bias recent locality.
- Queue signal: aggregate kernel queue depth + GPU decode backlog + observed token latency tail as single backpressure metric. Use double-threshold (soft/hard) to decide degrade actions.
- Actions: (a) soft: reduce prefill admission rate and increase coalescing window; (b) hard: prefill admission block for low reuse_score shards and opportunistically promote high reuse ones.
- Ghost protocol: when eviction removes a fragment, create a probabilistic tombstone record with small metadata (fingerprint, size, eviction_time). On subsequent prefill or decode that would request the fragment, consult tombstone; if tombstone hit and fragment size < threshold, perform partial rehydrate (on-device copy from remote cold store) instead of full prefill. Tombstones expire via TTL and are memory-bounded using a small reservoir sampler.
- Telemetry: expose reuse_score histogram, prefill-throttle-ratio, ghost-hit/miss counters, and eviction-retry latencies.
implementation_plan:
1) Add reuse_score calculator in kv-metrics module (2d). 2) Implement backpressure aggregation endpoint in runtime telemetry (3d). 3) Scheduler: priority layer that consults reuse_score + backpressure to decide prefill admission (5d). 4) Ghost tombstone store with reservoir sampler and TTL (3d). 5) Integrate partial rehydrate path with existing prefill worker (4d). 6) Tests, benchmarks, and rollout flag (3d). Total: 20d engineering.

Code pointers: runtime/kv/reuse_score.go, runtime/scheduler/prefill_controller.go, runtime/ghost/ tombstone_store.go (new), worker/partial_rehydrate.go.

Safety: feature gated, default off; will run in canary on dedicated clusters first.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for reuse_score math and boundary conditions.
- Integration: synthetic workloads combining short chats + large batched prefill to validate reduction in eviction storms.
- Performance: compare p99 decode latency and token cost on internal benchmark harness.
- Chaos: simulate slow network for cold store to verify graceful fallback to full prefill.
- Observability: dashboards for prefill-throttled percentage, ghost hits, and failed partial rehydrates.
- Rollout: start with 5% traffic, monitor errors & p99, expand to 50% then 100%.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Ghost tombstones might increase metadata memory pressure. Mitigation: reservoir sampler bounded to 1% of KV metadata memory and TTL of 10 minutes.
- Risk: Incorrect reuse_score bias could starve certain tenants. Mitigation: per-tenant lower bound and telemetry to detect starvation.
- Risk: Throttling too aggressively increases user-visible latency. Mitigation: double-threshold with opt-out for high-SLA tenants and quick rollback flag.
